summary: Completed the SkiaSharp host-compatibility spike for the Jellyfin 12 renderer (ADR-010). Confirmed from the pinned host's /tmp/opencode/jf/jellyfin/jellyfin.deps.json and native files that Jellyfin 12.0.0 pins SkiaSharp, SkiaSharp.HarfBuzz, and SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux at 3.119.4 and HarfBuzzSharp / HarfBuzzSharp.NativeAssets.Linux at 8.3.1.5, with native ELF64 x86-64 libSkiaSharp.so and libHarfBuzzSharp.so; the host's SkiaSharp managed and native files are byte-identical to the local NuGet 3.119.4 assets. Determined the plugin resolution answer by inspecting the pinned Jellyfin v12.0 source (Emby.Server.Implementations.Plugins.PluginLoadContext and PluginManager) and by empirically running Jellyfin's exact load-context pattern on the pinned .NET 10.0.12 runtime with a throwaway probe plugin: Jellyfin passes the plugin folder to AssemblyDependencyResolver (which does not discover a deps.json inside it) and then loads every DLL in the folder into the plugin load context; a plugin shipping no SkiaSharp resolves the host's shared managed SkiaSharp and native library, while a plugin shipping SkiaSharp.dll uses its own managed copy and finds libSkiaSharp.so only when it sits next to SkiaSharp.dll in the plugin folder root (x64/ and runtimes/linux-x64/native/ are not probed and fail with DllNotFoundException). The resulting Phase 5 constraint is to ship the managed and root-level native SkiaSharp assets in the plugin folder. Proved a genuine decode/draw/encode round trip on the pinned SkiaSharp 3.119.4 native library with the bundled DejaVu Sans Bold font loaded from embedded bytes, encoded as a non-interlaced 8-bit PNG and decoded back, via a committed environment-guarded test; the default suite reports it as skipped (439 passed, 1 skipped, 440 total) and the forced run with ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 and the pinned sysroot on the loader path passes both compatibility cases. Confirmed HarfBuzzSharp/SkiaSharp.HarfBuzz are not needed for ADR-009's single-line bounded labels, so the 4.7 omission stands. Recorded all findings, evidence, exact commands, and the Phase 5 validation list in docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md and updated docs/implementation-readiness.md, PLANS.md, README.md, and docs/changelog.md. No plugin production code was changed; full native-asset plugin packaging remains the Phase 5 task.

Fetched and inspected the pinned Jellyfin v12.0 source at commit 6c073e19ddf604b2369c638716164fdab4c952dc: Emby.Server.Implementations/Plugins/PluginLoadContext.cs (AssemblyLoadContext base(true), AssemblyDependencyResolver, Load returns plugin path or null) and Plugins/PluginManager.cs (constructs PluginLoadContext(plugin.Path) where LocalPlugin.Path is the plugin folder, then loads every DLL in the folder with LoadFromAssemblyPath before GetTypes).

Executed a throwaway .NET 10.0.12 harness replicating PluginLoadContext: AssemblyDependencyResolver(plugin DIRECTORY) returned null for both ResolveAssemblyToPath(SkiaSharp) and ResolveUnmanagedDllToPath(libSkiaSharp); AssemblyDependencyResolver(plugin DLL path) returned the plugin-local SkiaSharp.dll and runtimes/linux-x64/native/libSkiaSharp.so paths.

Executed throwaway load-context scenarios with a probe plugin: scenario A (no bundled SkiaSharp, host SkiaSharp preloaded) bound the host's /tmp/opencode/jf/jellyfin/SkiaSharp.dll in the default ALC and mapped the host's libSkiaSharp.so; scenario B (bundled SkiaSharp.dll + root libSkiaSharp.so) bound the plugin-local SkiaSharp.dll and mapped the plugin-local libSkiaSharp.so; scenario B with the native lib under x64/ or runtimes/linux-x64/native/ failed with DllNotFoundException; scenario C (host managed+native preloaded, then plugin bundled managed+native at root) mapped both libSkiaSharp.so copies and used the plugin-local one.

Ran the decode/draw/encode round trip on the pinned SkiaSharp 3.119.4 native library via the committed test: it decoded a synthetic 16x16 PNG, drew a scaled image plus an ADR-009-style pill and '1080p Blu-ray' text with the embedded DejaVu Sans Bold bytes, encoded a PNG, asserted the PNG signature and IHDR (240x360, bit depth 8, RGB/RGBA, zero compression/filter/interlace), and decoded the output back to 240x360.

known_limitations: No live Jellyfin host run was performed for this spike. The host artifacts and pinned Jellyfin source were inspected and the plugin load context was replicated on the exact pinned .NET runtime; the packaged-asset behavior on the live host is explicitly deferred to Phase 5 and listed in docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md section 3.5.

The load-context probe harness and probe plugin lived under /tmp/opencode and are not committed (per the spike's no-throwaway-artifacts boundary); the committed test covers only the AssemblyDependencyResolver-on-directory behavior and the round trip, and the full harness procedure/source is reproduced in Appendix A of docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md.
Only the linux-x64 RID and the pinned Ubuntu 24.04 sysroot were exercised; multi-RID packaging remains Phase 5 validation.

The round-trip proof is skipped by default because the default suite does not put the transitive libfontconfig.so.1 on the loader path; it must be run with ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 and the pinned sysroot on LD_LIBRARY_PATH, as recorded in the evidence doc.

The plugin package still does not ship the SkiaSharp managed/native assets or a dependency manifest; that remains the Phase 5 packaging task. No plugin production code or renderer service contract was added in 4.8.
